note: Canada issues no national identity card: in 2002 the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration asked Canadians to discuss the possibility of creating one, and the House of Commons committee that studied it reported against it in 2003; in January 2026 the federal government answered in Parliament that it is not implementing a federal or national digital identification credential. Provincial cards are left to the Canadian package, with the driver's licence.

sources.title: House of Commons Standing Committee on Citizenship and Immigration, A National Identity Card for Canada? (Sixth Report, 37th Parliament, 2nd Session, 2003)
sources.said: proposed that Canadians engage in a full and informed discussion about the possibility of creating a national identity card.

sources.title: MobileSyrup, federal government's written response on a national digital ID (30 January 2026)
sources.said: In response, the federal government said it’s “not implementing a federal or national digital identification credential.”
